cases.oracle: The guest setup compiles a deterministic two-thread fixture and runs parser controls plus a native sibling ptrace control, including complete syscall returns and natural thread exits. For each case, setup starts the actual candidate shell blocked on stdin and a separate owned tracee, verifies live distinct tasks, ownership, untraced state and closed shared-memory gates, then invokes -p on that same tracee. It samples per-TID TracerPid in both task orders before release, releases worker then leader only after worker exit, and records actual fixture and candidate status, timeout and raw stdout/stderr. Failed infrastructure checks fail setup; a valid completed fixture with a candidate mismatch is retained for candidate assessment. PR_SET_PTRACER authorizes only the candidate PID. The primary approved native oracle substitution is conditional on reviewed guest evidence and does not claim GNU strace equivalence. A bounded non-resumption after gate release is retained as candidate mismatch only when repeated live /proc snapshots show the original task in the same tracing stop, with unchanged context-switch counts and TracerPid equal to the owned live candidate. The observer records proof before killing the candidate for cleanup; any post-kill fixture result is explicitly distinguished from natural completion under tracing. Ambiguous stalls fail setup as inconclusive.
cases.purpose: Attach to an already-running owned process and trace until it exits naturally.
cases.comparison: Require the controlled invocation to have a complete setup record and native control, then a complete line-anchored leader getpid with its actual PID, followed by its zero exit event, leader attachment observation, zero candidate status, and empty candidate stdout. Reject tracer errors, incomplete records and missing final newline. An independently attributed non-resumption of a released task is a candidate mismatch, never a match.
cases.primary_evidence_gate: Primary must independently implement and review this data-only gate; generic runner labels alone are not evidence. Common inputs: setup result/status and timeout, setup-controls.json including stage events, parser-controls.json, stall-controls.json, gcc.out/gcc.err, native-control.json, candidate.out/candidate.err, fixture.out/fixture.err and assertions.json, including each diagnostic missing/error/truncation flag and raw bytes. For completed setup reject missing, malformed or truncated inputs; nonzero/timed-out setup; incomplete/error controls; failed parser or stall positive/negative controls; native nonzero statuses or raw native output inconsistent with controlled calls, return values, exits and markers; setup-controls lacking complete=true, invoked=true, candidate status/timeout, or valid initial [0,0,1,1] gates, two distinct original task IDs, task identity, common owner parentage, and initial TracerPid zero; or either candidate capture at the 512 KiB limit. For outcome=completed require worker and leader releases, worker disappearance before leader release, natural fixture exit zero before any candidate cleanup and exactly the two fixture markers with empty fixture stderr. Then independently parse complete candidate output against the recorded identities and check the case-specific ordered calls/exits, attachment samples and status; zero or partial attachment, or candidate timeout after independently confirmed natural fixture completion, is product mismatch, not infrastructure failure. For outcome=candidate_stall do not require natural fixture completion under the candidate, later leader release, full exit trace or newline: that would discard the very failure being assessed. Instead require worker_release and, for a leader stall, worker_gone_before_leader_release and leader_release; ordered monotonic stage events with release before wait, wait before timeout, observation after timeout and before all samples, and tracer cleanup after all samples; a wait of at least 4 s for worker or 5 s for leader; exactly three increasing samples spanning at least 200 ms; in every sample the original target and leader identities and owner parentage match preconditions, the owned candidate tracer remains alive with matching identity and parentage, fixture remains alive, target State is t (tracing stop), target TracerPid is that candidate, the target context-switch counters are unchanged, and gate words are [1,0,1,1] for worker or [1,1,1,1] for leader. Require the recorded cleanup to request tracer SIGKILL after observation with status -9, candidate_timeout=true and candidate_status_origin=cleanup_sigkill; retain its separate post-kill fixture status and any recovery actions, never describe them as a natural exit under tracing. A fully established stall is candidate mismatch even if post-kill fixture recovery is incomplete or the raw trace ends mid-record. A fixture-stage timeout that does not meet the stall predicate, missing stage records, vanished or running tasks, different tracers, changing context switches, missing live status, invalid pre-intervention gate data, failed observer or inability to reap owned processes are infrastructure/inconclusive, not product failure. For either outcome reject absent/malformed/truncated assertions, wrong requirement, infrastructure_error or disagreement with independent raw-data assessment. Successful setup with valid controls and an attributable stall must not be rejected merely because natural fixture completion or full trace text is absent. For failed setup retain stage-appropriate available diagnostics without treating missing later-stage files as product evidence. No GNU output equivalence is claimed.

cases.purpose: Attach the existing threads of the already-running process.
cases.comparison: Also require both original TIDs observed attached in successive opposite-order samples before release, a complete worker getppid returning the owner PID, worker zero exit before leader call, and no -f. Reject tracer errors, incomplete records and missing final newline. An independently attributed non-resumption of a released task is a candidate mismatch, never a match.
